input.quote: (h) This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of Nova Scotia and the laws of Canada applicable in Nova Scotia. All disputes under this Agreement shall be subject to the non-exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of Nova Scotia.
input.rationale: The governing law clause in Section 20 (General Matters) selects Nova Scotia (Canadian) law and the courts of Nova Scotia, which is the counterparty's home jurisdiction and is outside the accepted list of New York, Delaware, California, or England and Wales. The rule permits no non-listed jurisdiction, so we replaced only the jurisdiction and forum words with New York law and exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in New York County, leaving the remainder of the sentence intact. No arbitration provision appears elsewhere in the Agreement.

ops.oldText: This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of Nova Scotia and the laws of Canada applicable in Nova Scotia. All disputes under this Agreement shall be subject to the non-exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of Nova Scotia.
ops.newText: This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of the State of New York. All disputes under this Agreement shall be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts located in New York County, New York.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have changed the governing law and forum from Nova Scotia to New York law with exclusive jurisdiction in the state and federal courts in New York County, which is our standard position. If helpful, we can accept Delaware or California law and courts, or the laws of England and Wales with the courts of London.
proposal.summary: Replace Nova Scotia governing law and venue with New York law and exclusive New York County courts.
